**Derivation.**  
Write the angles at which $P$ sees the sides of $A_1B_1C_1D_1$:
$$\alpha_1=\angle PAB,\ \alpha_2=\angle PAD;\ \beta_1=\angle PBA,\ \beta_2=\angle PBC;\ \gamma_1=\angle PCB,\ \gamma_2=\angle PCD;\ \delta_1=\angle PDC,\ \delta_2=\angle PDA,$$
all acute by hypothesis.  
Because $A_2$ is the reflection of $P$ in $AB$, $\triangle A_2AB\cong\triangle PAB$; similarly $BA_2=BP=BB_2$ and $\angle A_2BB_2=2\beta$. From the isosceles triangles one obtains
$$\angle A_2=\alpha_2+\beta_2,\quad \angle B_2=\beta_2+\gamma_1,\quad \angle C_2=\gamma_2+\delta_1,\quad \angle D_2=\delta_1+\alpha_1,$$
and the ray $PA_2$ divides $\angle A_2$ into $\beta_2$ and $\alpha_2$ (and cyclically).  
Iterating the same computation gives
$$\begin{aligned}
&\angle A_3=\alpha_2+\gamma_1,\ \angle B_3=\beta_2+\delta_1,\ \angle C_3=\alpha_1+\gamma_2,\ \angle D_3=\beta_1+\delta_2,\\
&\angle A_4=\alpha_2+\delta_1,\ \angle B_4=\alpha_1+\beta_2,\ \angle C_4=\beta_1+\gamma_2,\ \angle D_4=\gamma_1+\delta_2,\\
&\angle A_5=\alpha_1+\alpha_2=\angle A_1,\ \text{etc.}
\end{aligned}$$
Hence the angle 4‑tuples repeat every four steps, so $A_{k+4}B_{k+4}C_{k+4}D_{k+4}\sim A_kB_kC_kD_k$. Since $1997\equiv1\pmod4$, among the first $12$ the similar ones are $k=1,5,9$.

For cyclicity, $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ is cyclic iff $(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)+(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)=180^\circ$ and $(\beta_1+\beta_2)+(\delta_1+\delta_2)=180^\circ$. Then
$$\angle A_3+\angle C_3=(\alpha_2+\gamma_1)+(\alpha_1+\gamma_2)=(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)+(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)=180^\circ,$$
and similarly $\angle B_3+\angle D_3=180^\circ$, so all odd-indexed quadrilaterals are cyclic. The even-indexed ones have opposite sums $(\alpha_2+\beta_2)+(\gamma_2+\delta_1)$ etc., which are not forced to $180^\circ$ (and fail generically), hence they are not cyclic.
